did: Home's cards essay on its database recorded every scene, then failed at the end: its cheat sheet had five rows, and the wide video's card holds fewer than five rows with notes in one column. Home then tried it again every hour, though it fails the same way each time. Now a cheat sheet that outgrows one column sets its rows in two, holds up to six rows (every essay so far has three to six), and all 73 sheets in the cards folder draw, this essay's too. A burn-in that doesn't fit the frame is now said the way home already holds a scene that doesn't fit, so it waits until the essay changes instead of retrying hourly; you agreed to that, and the ledger says so. The promise that a sheet is never refused for its count went through four fresh reviews; the first three found it false and each made it truer, one by fixing a row that fitted with its badge open but not shut.

calls.title: How a cheat sheet that outgrows one column is drawn, and how many rows it may hold
options: two columns in the wide frame and a bound of six rows
keep one column and lower the bound to four rows
shrink the sheet's type until its rows fit
keep eight rows and refuse what doesn't fit when it is recorded
calls.why: Six is the most rows two columns of the wide card hold with two-line notes, and every essay so far has three to six; four would refuse eighteen of them, and smaller type reads worse on a phone (C1400).
calls.undo: Record a call that moves C1400, set MOST_ROWS back and drop the second column in cheat-sheet.ts.

left: A burn-in refused for its words, such as a row that gives a value or a character the font lacks, is still tried again every hour though it never changes; #3452 proposes a one-line refusal shared with the asset recorder, and it needs a change to home's render worker.

The weekly call, Playoff Delta and Rust Rounds essays now hold a burn-in that doesn't fit too, since they share the recorder, but their ledger objectives (CW5, PK5, EV2) still name only too long or too large; the coordinator put that to you on #3452.

In the wide frame, a row whose command can't sit beside its task in half the card draws only while its sheet fits one column; with more rows it is refused by its number. No essay so far has such a row.
